A chi-square test of independence on the male-by-partner eye color table gives χ² = 33.70 with 4 degrees of freedom and p ≈ 8.6e-7. That is strong evidence against independence.

Matches on the diagonal are more common than chance would give. Blue-eyed men most often have blue-eyed partners (78 of 114), and the brown–brown and green–green counts are also high. So eye colors do not look independent.

ANSWER: no
